clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11181 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime indusiry". This order (29 FR 13557, Federal Register of October 2, 1964, signed September 30, 1964) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Herbert Schmertz as chairman, James J. Healy and Theodore W. Kheel) to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before Thursday, October 1, 1964; and provided that upon the submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the order's own continuing-existence sentence means its text does not end the Board when the report is submitted. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 13557, the issue of October 2, 1964) is Executive Order 11181, dated September 30, 1964; the order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 for labor disputes affecting the maritime industry, and carries the signature date September 30, 1964. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself, not of this order, and the dispute was a one-time dispute. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.
